options.meaning: One website adapts its structure, controls, and content priority to mobile screens and input.

consequences.device-features: Browser-supported device features are available, while deep native integration is limited.
consequences.app-store-requirements: The product is delivered by URL and does not require app-store review.
consequences.offline-behavior: Selective caching and draft preservation are possible, but full offline behavior needs deliberate web support.
consequences.performance: Ordinary product flows can perform well when the current web application is kept lean.
consequences.current-codebase: The current web codebase and routing can be adapted instead of replaced.
consequences.team-ability: The team can use its existing web skills and testing practices.
consequences.budget: This path normally adds the least platform-specific build and review work.
consequences.maintenance: One shared codebase and release path remain the main maintenance surface.
consequences.desired-experience: The experience is linkable and broadly available, with less native platform character.

options.meaning: One mobile application codebase targets iOS and Android and is distributed through app stores.

consequences.device-features: A framework bridge can expose many device capabilities, with platform-specific work for gaps.
consequences.app-store-requirements: App-store packaging, review, signing, and release operations become required.
consequences.offline-behavior: Local application storage can support deeper offline workflows with explicit synchronization design.
consequences.performance: Most product flows can perform well, while intensive platform behavior may need native modules.
consequences.current-codebase: Some product logic may be reused, but interface and platform integration need a mobile application layer.
consequences.team-ability: The team needs framework, device, signing, and store-release competence.
consequences.budget: Shared application code reduces duplication but adds mobile tooling, testing, and release cost.
consequences.maintenance: One shared mobile layer still carries iOS, Android, framework, and store maintenance.
consequences.desired-experience: The result can feel application-like while retaining some framework constraints.

options.meaning: Separate native iOS or Android applications use each platform's own language, frameworks, and interface conventions.

consequences.device-features: The deepest platform integration and newest native APIs are available directly.
consequences.app-store-requirements: Each platform needs its own signing, review, release, and compliance work.
consequences.offline-behavior: Native storage and background behavior can support advanced offline requirements.
consequences.performance: Native code offers direct control for demanding graphics, sensors, or low-latency behavior.
consequences.current-codebase: The web interface cannot be reused directly and shared business logic needs an explicit boundary.
consequences.team-ability: The team needs platform-specific engineering, testing, and release skill.
consequences.budget: Separate platform work creates the highest build and staffing cost when both platforms are required.
consequences.maintenance: Each platform, release train, and native dependency must be maintained over time.
consequences.desired-experience: The product can match platform conventions most closely and use native behavior without a bridge.
